Every kit exposes **one theme value** with the same field names, cased for the language
(`colorScheme` in TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin; `color_scheme` in Python and GDScript). Every field
is optional. An empty theme is the Polaris Key look in the product's accent.

## The theme

| Field         | Values                                                                           | Default                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `preset`      | `"polaris-key"` · `"native"`                                                     | `"polaris-key"`                                      | The base look ([the native preset](#the-native-preset))                                                                                                    |
| `colorScheme` | `"system"` · `"dark"` · `"light"`                                                | `"system"`; `"dark"` for Godot and TV                | Follows the OS live, and is dark when the OS has no preference. Games follow their own art, so the Godot kit defaults to dark                              |
| `accent`      | `"product"` · `"core"` · `"service"` · a colour                                  | `"product"`                                          | The product's colour, else one derived from its icon, else ink; `"core"` is Polaris violet. Every value goes through the [resolver](#the-accent-resolver)  |
| `serviceCues` | boolean                                                                          | `false`                                              | Service glyph tiles on settings group headers; implied by `accent: "service"`                                                                              |
| `colors`      | a partial map of semantic roles (`surfacePage`, `textStrong`, `danger`, …)       | none                                                 | Per-role overrides, per scheme (`colors.dark`, `colors.light`)                                                                                             |
| `radius`      | `"sm"` · `"md"` · `"lg"` · a number                                              | `"md"`                                               | The control radius; surfaces scale from it. On the web, `sm` is 6/10, `md` 12/22 and `lg` 16/28 (control/card)                                             |
| `typography`  | `family`, `display`, `monoFamily`, `scale`                                       | Rubik (`"inherit"` when embedded), the kit mono, 1.0 | `family: "system"` uses the platform face and `"inherit"` the host's; `display` sets a heading face (games); `scale` multiplies on top of the OS text size |
| `density`     | `"compact"` · `"comfortable"` · `"spacious"`                                     | `"comfortable"`; `"spacious"` for Godot and TV       | Control height and spacing only, never the component                                                                                                       |
| `motion`      | `"system"` · `"reduced"` · `"none"`                                              | `"system"`                                           | `system` follows the OS reduced-motion setting                                                                                                             |
| `ambient`     | boolean                                                                          | `true` (`false` under `native`)                      | The product's own icon or art, blurred behind the gate and boot screens                                                                                    |
| `product`     | `ProductIdentity`                                                                | from the presentation, then the bundle               | [Product identity](/docs/build/ui/#product-identity), including `shortName`, `wordmark` and `deviceCodeUrl`                                                |
| `copy`        | a partial map of copy keys, or a `locale`                                        | the OS locale                                        | [Localisation](/docs/build/ui/localisation/#overriding-copy)                                                                                               |
| `poweredBy`   | `false` · `"line"` · `"badge"`                                                   | `false`                                              | The optional "Powered by Polaris Key" line or badge, at the foot of settings and about screens only                                                        |
| `platform`    | `"auto"` · `"ios"` · `"android"` · `"macos"` · `"windows"` · `"linux"` · `"web"` | `"auto"`                                             | Web and Qt Quick kits render that platform's variant inside a webview or QML (Electron on Windows gets Fluent, Tauri on macOS gets the Mac sheet)          |

## Where each kit takes it

Each kit fills its tab when it ships this theme API. Until then the tab shows the planned entry
point and links to the kit's current docs.

<Tabs syncKey="ui-kit">
  <TabItem label="React">
    <KitPending kits={["react"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `<PolarisKeyProvider theme={…}>`, or the `polarisKeyTheme({ … })` helper.
    Beyond the theme: the stable `pk-*` class names and `data-part` attributes, all inside the
    `@layer polaris-key` cascade layer so host CSS wins without `!important`; slots and render
    props; and `--pk-*` variables scoped to the provider element, never `:root`. React and the web
    components share one `styles.css` and one `data-part` contract.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Web components">
    <KitPending kits={["elements"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `<pk-provider theme='…'>`, `PolarisKey.theme({ … })`, or `--pk-*` custom
    properties. Beyond the theme: `::part(title)`, `::part(primary)` and the other parts, named
    slots, `pk-*` DOM events, and the shared `styles.css` adopted into each shadow root.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Vue, Svelte, Angular">
    <KitPending kits={["vue", "svelte", "angular"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `providePolarisKey({ theme })` in Vue and Angular, `setPolarisKeyTheme` in
    Svelte. Each passes the web components' parts and slots through.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="SwiftUI">
    <KitPending kits={["swiftui"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** the `.polarisKeyTheme(PolarisKeyTheme(…))` environment modifier. Beyond the
    theme: a style protocol per component (`.activateStyle(.myStyle)`), in the manner of
    `ButtonStyle`, and `@ViewBuilder` slots.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="UIKit, AppKit">
    <KitPending kits={["uikit", "appkit"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `PolarisKeyUI.theme = …`, or a theme per presenter. Beyond the theme:
    subclassable hosting controllers.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Compose">
    <KitPending kits={["compose"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `PolarisKeyTheme(theme = PolarisKeyTheme(…)) { }`. Beyond the theme:
    `ActivateDefaults.colors()`, `shapes()` and the other `*Defaults` objects, like Material's
    `ButtonDefaults`, and composable slot parameters.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Godot">
    <KitPending kits={["godot"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `ui_theme_preset`, `ui_accent`, `ui_radius`, `ui_density` and the other `ui_*`
    options in `polaris_key.tres`, or `PKeyUiTheme.build(theme)`. Beyond the theme: documented
    theme type variations (`PKeyTitle`, `PKeyPrimary`, …); a per-node `Theme` wins.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Qt">
    <KitPending kits={["qt"]} what="this theme API" />

    **Planned:** `polaris_key.ui.qt.apply_theme(app, Theme(…))`. Beyond the theme: object names
    (`#pkTitle`, `#pkPrimary`) and dynamic properties for QSS, and the native `QStyle` under the
    `native` preset.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Terminal">
    <KitPending
      kits={["terminal-node", "terminal-python"]}
      what="this theme API"
    />

    **Planned:** `PolarisKeyTheme` in the CLI adapter's options, `PKEY_THEME=dark` or `light`, and
    `NO_COLOR`. Beyond the theme: a unicode or ascii symbol set.

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## The accent resolver

One algorithm in `@polaris-key/brand` (`resolveAccent`), ported to Swift, Kotlin, GDScript and
Python, turns any input colour into the five colours a kit draws with, for each scheme. It adjusts
OKLCH lightness only:

- **`solid`**, the primary's fill: at least 3:1 on every surface;
- **`fg`**, accent text and icons: at least 4.5:1 on every surface;
- **`subtle`**, the tinted fill of a selected row;
- **`focus`**, the focus ring;
- **`on`**, the primary's label: at least 4.5:1 on `solid`. It prefers white, so the label is
  the same in both schemes; only light accents (yellows, oranges, light teals) flip to an ink
  label, again in both schemes.

When the product supplies no colour, `deriveAccent` picks one from the icon: the most saturated
colour that covers at least 8 % of the icon's opaque area, or nothing for a near-greyscale icon,
which falls through to ink. Status colours never change with the accent.

The resolver's output for the specification's examples, read from the shared test vectors every
port must reproduce exactly (`packages/brand/fixtures/accent-vectors.json`):

## The native preset

`preset: "native"` keeps the structure, flows, copy and spacing and hands the look to the host:

- **Web:** the host's font (`font: inherit`), `Canvas` and `CanvasText` neutrals, the host's accent
  from `theme.accent`, else its `accent-color`, else the CSS `AccentColor` system colour; radii from
  the host; no ambient. It never hard-codes a platform blue.
- **SwiftUI, UIKit and AppKit:** system fonts, the app's `.tint`, system colours and materials,
  stock button styles.
- **Compose:** the host's `MaterialTheme`, dynamic colour included, with the status colours mapped
  to the host scheme's error and a computed warning.
- **Godot:** derived from the ancestor or project theme.
- **Qt:** the platform `QStyle` (or the Qt Quick native style), with only spacing and the type
  hierarchy applied.

## Bring your own design system

There are no separate kits for host design systems. The brand package publishes presets and theme
objects for them instead, and each screen can be rendered with host components over the headless
layer. They are listed on [Recipes](/docs/build/ui/recipes/).
